children: Fitch Credit Ratings upgraded Sri Lanka's long-term foreign currency credit rating to ´B-' from 'CCC+' on September 22, 2026, citing progress in macroeconomic stabilization and structural reforms, which have reduced external financing risks.
The agency pointed to sharp improvements in fiscal and external balances and a modest rebuilding of foreign exchange reserves.
Fitch expects fiscal discipline and revenue mobilization to support sustained primary surpluses, helping keep government debt on a downward path and reducing the risk of renewed external imbalances.
Primary surpluses are expected to remain above 2% of GDP, with government debt falling to 92.9% of GDP in 2026 from 96.7% in 2025.
However, debt and debt-servicing ratios remain high compared with rating peers, while FX reserve buffers remain modest as external debt servicing is expected to rise over the next five year.

title: Fitch Upgrades Sri Lanka's Credit Rating to B-
